title: Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Peering Health
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Peering Health' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_internet_exchange_point_ixp_peering_health` (UC-5.10.14), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Peering Health", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-5.10.14 positive (Internet, Exchange, Point, (IXP), Peering): ingest synthetic events into `index=network` sourcetype='cisco:ios' where `bad_samples`, `state_entropy` grouped by `_time`, `ix_name`, `peer`, `asn_peer` satisfies `bad_samples` > 0, or `state_entropy` > 3 for 'Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Peering Health'. Validate lookup `ix_peering_neighbors.csv`. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-5.10.14 negative (Peering Health): ingest benign `network` / `cisco:ios` events where `_time`, `ix_name`, `peer`, `asn_peer` stays below `bad_samples` > 0, or `state_entropy` > 3, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv`. Variant 3 confirms zero alert rows for 'Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Peering Health'.

dataSources: `index=network` BGP syslog (`sourcetype=cisco:ios`, `sourcetype=juniper:junos`) filtered to peers documented in `ix_peering_neighbors.csv` (`neighbor_ip`, `ix_name`, `ix_lan`, `asn_peer`, `route_server_flag`). NetFlow (`index=netflow`) toward IX-facing interfaces optionally supplements traffic-plane visibility via lookup `ix_interfaces.csv` mapping exporter/interface tuples. Collected via Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `TA-cisco_ios`, `Splunk_TA_juniper`, optional NetFlow TA. — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=network earliest=-4h (sourcetype="cisco:ios" OR sourcetype="juniper:junos")
    ("%BGP-5-ADJCHANGE" OR "%BGP-3-NOTIFICATION" OR "BGP_PEER_UP" OR "BGP_PEER_DOWN" OR "Notification sent")
| rex field=_raw "neighbor (?<peer>[0-9a-fA-F:\.:\]]+)"
| lookup ix_peering_neighbors.csv neighbor_ip as peer OUTPUT ix_name asn_peer route_server_flag
| where isnotnull(ix_name)
| rex field=_raw "(?i)(?<transition>(?:Established|Idle|Active|Connect|OpenSent|Down)[^\n]*)"
| eval unhealthy=if(match(transition,"(?i)Idle|Active|Connect|Down|Notification"),1,0)
| bin _time span=30m
| stats sum(unhealthy) as bad_samples count as msgs dc(transition) as state_entropy values(transition) as last_states by _time ix_name peer asn_peer route_server_flag host
| where bad_samples>0 OR state_entropy>3
| stats latest(bad_samples) as alerts latest(msgs) as chatter latest(last_states) as transitions latest(route_server_flag) as rs_mode by ix_name peer asn_peer host
| sort -alerts
description: Monitors when Peering Health criteria fire for 'Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Peering Health' (UC-5.10.14) in `index=network` sourcetype `cisco:ios`. Pipeline aggregates `bad_samples`, `state_entropy` by `_time`, `ix_name`, `peer`, `asn_peer` over `30m`. Alert logic enforces `bad_samples` > 0, or `state_entropy` > 3. SPL signature: lookup `ix_peering_neighbors.csv`. Eliminates manual hunting for UC-5.10.14 conditions.
value: UC-5.10.14 helps teams contain Internet, Exchange, Point, (IXP), Peering scenarios and reduce operational risk and delayed incident response before incidents compound.
implementation: Maintain gold-standard CSV whenever peers move ports; annotate route-server vs bilateral peers to tune thresholds; integrate IX participant portal outage RSS optional enrichment.
visualization: Per-IX bubble chart (peer ASN vs flap score); timeline bands colored by IX fabric outage hypotheses; table linking peer IPs to MAC addresses when ARP logs exist.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `network` (UC-5.10.14)** — Planned work for 'Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Peering Health' shifts `bad_samples`, `state_entropy` over `span=30m` while `_time`, `ix_name`, `peer`, `asn_peer` remains in-scope. Applies lookup `ix_peering_neighbors.csv`. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `sum` on `cisco:ios`** — Scheduled automation elevates `ix_name` without crossing `bad_samples` > 0 for UC-5.10.14. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `_time`, `ix_name`, `peer`, `asn_peer`** — Health checks in `network` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `cisco:ios`** — First 48h baseline for UC-5.10.14 on `_time` is unstable; join `ix_peering_neighbors.csv` prior to threshold.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `_time`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Accurate neighbor-to-IX mapping refreshed after every IX migration.
• Understanding bilateral versus route-server operational expectations (RS peers tolerate controlled resets).
• Clock sync across route reflectors logging duplicates.
• Optional NetFlow validation proving traffic collapse aligns with control-plane logs.

Step 1 — Import `ix_peering_neighbors.csv` via automation consuming IRR/peering DB exports plus manual overrides.

Step 2 — Tune rex statements per Junos `RPD_BGP_NEIGHBOR_STATE_CHANGED` vs Cisco `%BGP-5-ADJCHANGE` formats.

Step 3 — Severity matrix flags RS peers differently—idle/connect churn may indicate LAN duplex mismatch.

Step 4 — Dashboard overlays IX LAN SNMP errors (from UC-5.1.x physical monitors) when BGP alerts fire.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting: duplicate syslog paths inflate counts—dedup via `dedup` on signature hash; private interconnect VLAN tagging mistakes misassociate peers—verify CMDB.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`TA-cisco_ios`, `Splunk_TA_juniper`, optional NetFlow TA. — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ios, juniper:junos into network. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, asn_peer, bad_samples, host`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
